timing.label: Slack update to the support lead (≤120 words, spoken in 90 s)
Objection 1 (technical)
timing.question: Who is accountable when the bot posts a wrong diagnosis?

timing.label: Objection 2 (commercial)
timing.question: My team will stop reading the channel if the bot posts every time.

approach.quote: I picked the Triage Bug Reports one and, uh, pointed it at the channel

tag_question_examples: They'll get used to it, right?

must_mention.point: Repeated double-charge reports are grouped into one issue linked to the first report's thread, not answered each time
A shared scratchpad keeps triaged reports with channel, timestamp and reporter, the duplicates and the routing table
must_mention.evidence_quote: it keeps the triaged reports, the duplicates and the routing table

must_mention.point: A routing correction replied in the thread updates the routing table so later reports go to the right owner
The diagnosis is written back once in the original thread with the owner tagged, and repeats only get a reaction
Channel messages are untrusted input, so the responder runs under a network policy allowlist that blocks other hosts
The same setup runs on a Microsoft Teams channel through a Teams trigger, without private channels
must_mention.evidence_quote: It runs on a Microsoft Teams channel through a Teams trigger as well

sentences_to_rerecord: Update: the bot is live in #harbourline-bugs and replies to every message so nothing is missed.
Devin is accountable, it decides the refund, actually.
It answered the pasted ticket too, basically it did what it said.

accuracy.anchor: Two of six points, both hedged; claims the bot replies to every message and followed the pasted ticket. (anchors: 27–30 every point tied to a count, setting or file; 15–20 four of six; under 10 two or fewer)

structure.anchor: A tour of the Automations page; no outcome, no evidence, no ask. (anchors: 22–25 all parts in order; 13–17 parts present but weak; under 8 problem only)

customer_relevance.anchor: Nothing about what the support team will see; "they can mute it" works against the brief. (anchors: 16–20 answered in terms of what the support team sees, with counts; 10–13 some; under 6 feature talk)

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: Every segment off target, two long silences and eleven fillers. (anchors: 11–15 segments on target, under 1 filler/min; 6–8 two or more segments off; under 4 most segments off)

recovery.anchor: Objection 1 handed the refund decision to Devin (capped); objection 2 had no count and no pattern. (anchors: 7–10 acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer held with numbers; 4–6 partial; under 3 no pattern)

stems: "Your team will see one answer per problem…" — start from the support lead's channel, not the template list.
"Repeats get…" — say what a duplicate report gets instead of a reply.
"The owner confirms before…" — keep refunds and fixes with the tagged team.
previous_run_comparison: First recorded run for dryrun on lab 08; no previous run to compare with.
